free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'Many Microsoft product teams grant Azure credits to open source communities to support their work', but 'Microsoft is not accepting new applications from projects directly and is instead relying on strategic, organic relationships between Microsoft businesses and the open source that they depend on', and 'The application form is not currently open'.

chaining: This closes the Microsoft lane for an individual and leaves GitHub as the only Microsoft-owned route that still takes applications, which is why the GitHub Secure Open Source Fund record carries the Azure credits instead.

limits.value: There is no application route at all: an award now depends on a Microsoft product team choosing a project it already depends on, which no individual can initiate.

notes: Recorded as fails-identity rather than dead because grants are still being issued: the programme changed from an open form to relationship-based allocation, and a reader who finds only the 2021 blog post will believe the form is open. That divergence between a 2021 announcement and the 2026 landing page is the finding. Microsoft's FOSS Fund, named on the same page, is an internal employee-directed fund and has no external application.
